ei.title: Prior Knowledge as the X-Factor in Reading
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is (A)[highlighted / overlooked] in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of (B)[struggling / talented] readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored (C)[lower / higher]? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① highlighted - struggling - higher = 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② overlooked: '간과된'은 '강조된'이라는 원문과 반대
❌ ③ talented: '재능 있는'은 '어려움을 겪는'이라는 원문과 반대
❌ ④ lower: '더 낮은'은 어려움을 겪는 독자가 더 높은 점수를 받았다는 원문과 반대

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was (A)[composed / deprived] of struggling readers who were (B)[knowledgeable / ignorant] about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge (C)[enabled / prevented] them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① deprived/ignorant: '박탈된'과 '무지한'은 원문의 '구성된'과 '지식이 풍부한'과 각각 반대
❌ ② prevented: '막았다'는 사전 지식이 높은 점수를 받게 '해주었다'는 원문과 반대
✅ ③ composed - knowledgeable - enabled = 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ deprived/enabled: '박탈된'은 원문과 불일치
det.tip: composed of=~으로 구성된, knowledgeable=지식이 풍부한, enabled=가능하게 했다

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study (A)[consisted / lacked] of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not (B)[enough / excessive] for the students who came to the page with a knowledge (C)[deficit / surplus] about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① lacked: '부족했다'는 '~으로 구성되었다'는 원문과 의미가 다름
❌ ② surplus: '잉여'는 '부족'이라는 원문과 반대
❌ ③ excessive: '과도한'은 '충분한'이라는 원문과 의미가 다름
✅ ④ consisted - enough - deficit = 원문 일치 ←정답

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of ①<u>strong</u> readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of ②<u>struggling</u> readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge ③<u>abundance</u> about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better ④<u>abilities</u>. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① strong: '강한 독자'로 독해력이 뛰어난 학생 → 적절
❌ ② struggling: '어려움을 겪는 독자'로 독해력이 약한 학생 → 적절
✅ ③ abundance: '풍부'는 지식 '부족(deficit)'이라는 원문과 정반대 ←정답
❌ ④ abilities: '훨씬 뛰어난 능력'을 가진 독자 → 적절

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is ①<u>highlighted</u> in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were ②<u>knowledgeable</u> about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge ③<u>prevented</u> them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the ④<u>x-factor</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①highlighted(강조된) ②knowledgeable(지식이 풍부한) ③prevented(막았다←enabled) ④x-factor(결정적 요인)
det.analysis:
❌ ① highlighted: 연구에서 '강조된' → 적절
❌ ② knowledgeable: 야구에 대해 '지식이 풍부한' → 적절
✅ ③ prevented: '막았다'는 사전 지식이 높은 점수를 받을 수 있게 '해주었다(enabled)'는 원문과 정반대 ←정답
❌ ④ x-factor: 사전 지식이 '결정적 요인'이었다 → 적절

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of ①<u>proficient</u> readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their ②<u>comprehension</u> tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their ③<u>prior</u> knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the ④<u>x-factor</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① proficient: '능숙한 독자'는 '어려움을 겪는(struggling) 독자'라는 원문과 정반대. 두 번째 그룹은 독해력이 약한 학생임 ←정답
❌ ② comprehension: 각 그룹의 '이해력' 테스트 → 적절
❌ ③ prior: '사전' 지식이 높은 점수를 받게 해줌 → 적절
❌ ④ x-factor: 사전 지식이 '결정적 요인' → 적절

det.korean: 야구에 대해 ____한 독자들: 어려움을 겪지만 야구 지식은 풍부
det.analysis:
❌ ① curious: '호기심 있는'은 지식이 풍부하다는 의미가 아님
❌ ② indifferent: '무관심한'은 야구 지식과 무관
✅ ③ knowledgeable: '지식이 풍부한'은 야구에 대해 잘 아는 독자라는 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ suspicious: '의심하는'은 지식 수준과 무관

det.korean: 주제에 대한 지식 ____을 가진 학생들에게 독해 기술만으로는 부족
det.analysis:
❌ ① mastery: '숙달'은 독해력은 강하지만 야구를 모르는 학생에게 부적합
❌ ② surplus: '잉여'는 지식이 부족한 맥락에 맞지 않음
❌ ③ advantage: '이점'은 부족함을 나타내지 못함
✅ ④ deficit: '부족'은 주제에 대한 지식이 부족한 학생이라는 원문과 일치 ←정답

det.korean: 사전 지식이 그들을 훨씬 뛰어난 능력의 독자보다 ____하게 해주었다
det.analysis:
✅ ① outscore: '더 높은 점수를 받다'는 사전 지식 덕분에 능가했다는 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ② assist: '돕다'는 독자들을 돕는 것이 아니라 능가하는 맥락
❌ ③ imitate: '모방하다'는 점수와 무관
❌ ④ follow: '따르다'는 능가하는 맥락과 다름

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 highlighted와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① ignored: '무시된'은 highlighted의 반의어
✅ ② emphasized: '강조된'은 highlighted와 동의어 ←정답
❌ ③ questioned: '의문시된'은 강조와 다른 의미
❌ ④ concealed: '숨겨진'은 highlighted의 반의어

det.analysis:
❌ ① written: '쓰여진'은 composed의 다른 의미
✅ ② made up: 'made up of'는 'composed of'와 동의어 ←정답
❌ ③ divided: '나누어진'은 구성되었다는 의미가 아님
❌ ④ gathered: '모인'은 구성되었다는 의미와 다름
det.tip: be composed of ≈ be made up of (구성되다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 struggling과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

❌ ② weak: '약한'은 struggling과 유사한 의미
❌ ③ helpless: '무력한'은 struggling과 유사한 의미

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 Deficit과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① shortage: '부족'은 deficit과 동의어
✅ ② surplus: '잉여/초과'는 deficit(부족)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ③ scarcity: '희소성'은 deficit과 유사한 의미
❌ ④ weakness: '약점'은 부족과 다른 범주

questions.passage:
(A) The importance of what a reader <u>brings</u> to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit.

(B) She asked her friend to <u>bring</u> some snacks to the party this weekend.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 bring(s)의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 운반하다/(B) 기여하다: 의미가 뒤바뀜
✅ ② (A) 기여하다 - (B) 가져오다: 독자가 사전 지식을 '기여하다'(추상), 친구가 과자를 '가져오다'(구체) ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 기여하다/(B) 초래하다: 과자를 초래하는 것은 부적절
❌ ④ (A) 초래하다/(B) 가져오다: 독자가 지식을 초래하는 것은 부적절

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a shortage or lack of something, especially money or knowledge"

det.korean: 무언가, 특히 돈이나 지식의 부족 = deficit(결핍)

❌ ② advantage: '이점'은 부족이 아님
❌ ③ surplus: '잉여'는 부족의 반대
❌ ④ ability: '능력'은 부족과 무관

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was __________.
